reason: The text demonstrates that Yahweh cares deeply about and shows empathy for the Israelite people as a collective body. The entire passage describes God's direct action to rescue בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל (the people/children of Israel) from destruction. God: (1) commands them to advance fearlessly ('why do you cry to me?'); (2) performs the miraculous division of the sea specifically for their safe passage; (3) provides protective barriers of water on both sides ('וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חֹמָה'); (4) ensures their complete safe crossing ('וִיחַדְּלוּ בְתוֹךְ הַיָּם בַּיַּבָּשָׁה'). While Moses is used as the instrumental leader through whom God works, this demonstrates God's concern for the people's welfare, not indifference to them. The entire narrative shows empathy manifested through protective action for the collective people, not mere utilization of their leader.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
